profile.summary: DPLM-2 is a protein language model that handles sequence and structure in one model. Backbone coordinates are turned into discrete tokens by a quantising structure tokeniser, so a protein becomes one token string of amino acids and structure tokens, and a discrete diffusion language model is trained over both. From that single model come sequence and structure co-generation, folding (structure from sequence), inverse folding (sequence from structure) and motif scaffolding. Checkpoints are released at 150M, 650M and 3B parameters, plus a bit-based variant.

summary_quotes.text: we introduce DPLM-2, a multimodal protein foundation model that extends discrete diffusion protein language model (DPLM) to accommodate both sequences and structures.
To enable structural learning with the language model, 3D coordinates are converted to discrete tokens using a lookup-free quantization-based tokenizer.

enabling protein
sequence-structure co-generation and conditional generation tasks such as
folding, inverse folding, and motif scaffolding.

sections.title: How it works
sections.body: The 650M checkpoint is an ESM-style transformer with 33 layers, hidden size 1280 and 20 attention heads, loaded by the class EsmForDPLM2. What makes it multimodal is the vocabulary: 8,229 tokens covering amino acids, structure tokens and special tokens. Structure tokens come from a separate structure tokeniser, published as airkingbd/struct_tokenizer, which also rebuilds a PDB file from tokens. Training is discrete diffusion over this joint vocabulary, and it starts from a pretrained DPLM sequence model, a warm-up strategy the authors use to carry evolutionary knowledge into structure modelling. The README adds that DPLM-2 does inverse folding by conditioning directly on structure tokens, where the earlier DPLM used an adapter on top of the language model.

quotes.text:
- **Vocabulary:** 8,229 tokens, covering amino-acid tokens, structure tokens,
  and special tokens

- **Structure tokenizer:** Uses the DPLM structure tokenizer
  (`airkingbd/struct_tokenizer`) for structure-token based modeling and PDB
  reconstruction

We also implement an efficient warm-up strategy to exploit the connection between large-scale evolutionary data and structural inductive biases from pre-trained sequence-based protein language models.
DPLM-2 directly conditions on the tokenized structure tokens to predict the sequence.

sections.title: Versions and reproducibility
sections.body: Four checkpoints answered on Hugging Face: dplm2_150m, dplm2_650m, dplm2_3b and dplm2_bit_650m, the last being the finer-grained bit-based variant from the follow-up work the authors call DPLM-2.1. All are Apache-2.0 and none is gated. Decoding settings matter as much as the checkpoint: the README's inverse folding and folding commands use 100 iterations with deterministic unmasking and argmax sampling, and a July 2025 note says the default sampling strategy of DPLM-2 was changed to annealing@2.0:0.1. The HyInv report evaluated DPLM-2 3B at argmax decoding over 100 steps in BF16 autocast, and notes that with deterministic unmasking two designs of the same chain are almost always the same sequence.

sections.title: Training data
sections.body: Training uses experimental structures from the PDB together with AlphaFold2 predicted structures from SwissProt, published as the preprocessed dataset airkingbd/pdb_swissprot. The model is initialised from a pretrained DPLM checkpoint, and LoRA is used to keep the parameters from shifting far, with about 64,000 tokens per batch for 100,000 training steps. The bit-based variant uses the same data.

run_guide.summary: Install the DPLM codebase and design sequences for tokenised backbones with the 650M DPLM-2 checkpoint.
prerequisites: Conda with Python 3.9 and the repository's install script.
A GPU: the loading examples move the model to CUDA.
Backbone structures. The repository ships the tokenised CAMEO 2022 and PDB date test splits; your own PDB files must be tokenised first.

steps.title: Get the code and create the environment
steps.shell:
git clone --recursive https://github.com/bytedance/dplm.git
cd dplm

conda create -n dplm python=3.9 pip
conda activate dplm
bash scripts/install.sh
steps.explanation: Copied from the model card's Quick Start block. from byprot.models.dplm2 import MultimodalDiffusionProteinLanguageModel as DPLM2

dplm2 = DPLM2.from_pretrained("airkingbd/dplm2_650m").cuda()

steps.title: Design sequences for the tokenised test structures
steps.shell:
model_name=dplm2_650m
output_dir=generation-results/${model_name}
task=inverse_folding

mkdir -p ${output_dir}

input_fasta_path=data-bin/cameo2022/struct.fasta
python generate_dplm2.py \
    --model_name airkingbd/${model_name} \
    --task ${task} \
    --input_fasta_path ${input_fasta_path} \
    --max_iter 100 \
    --unmasking_strategy deterministic \
    --sampling_strategy argmax \
    --saveto ${output_dir}

# Evaluation
input_fasta_dir=${output_dir}/inverse_folding
python src/byprot/utils/protein/evaluator_dplm2.py -cn inverse_folding inference.input_fasta_dir=${input_fasta_dir}
steps.explanation: Copied from the README's Inverse Folding with DPLM-2 block, unchanged.

steps.title: Tokenise your own structures first
steps.shell:
# each protein is represented by a pdb file
input_pdb_folder=/path/to/your/input/structure
# this will save two fasta files in the ${input_pdb_folder}/tokenized_protein folder:
# 1) struct.fasta, containing the tokenized structure tokens
# 2) aatype.fasta, containing the amino acid tokens.
python src/byprot/utils/protein/tokenize_pdb.py --input_pdb_folder ${input_pdb_folder} --output_dir ${input_pdb_folder}/tokenized_protein
steps.explanation: Copied from the README's tokenisation block. The resulting struct.fasta is what the previous step takes as input_fasta_path.

notes: Points for a reviewer. The parameter counts in the structured rows are the round figures from the checkpoint names and the 650M model card; the Hugging Face API returned no safetensors totals, so none is exact, and the 150M, 3B and bit rows rest on the names alone. No release dates are published for the checkpoints, so released is null everywhere. The HyInv record names DPLM-2 3B, while the repository's own examples and the only model card read are for 650M; the structured rows cover both. This record sits beside a separate DPLM record for the sequence-only model in the same repository, which shares the README and the licence file. Quotes from the HyInv report come from a pdftotext text layer, so line breaks inside them follow the PDF layout.
